subject: general
question: A force F acts on a body of mass m producing acceleration a . If the force is 3 F and mass of the body is reduced to m/2 . What is the value of new acceleration in terms of 'a'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**6 a**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion** provides the fundamental relationship between **force**, **mass**, and **acceleration**. It states that the **acceleration** of an object is directly proportional to the net **force** acting on it and inversely proportional to its **mass**.
 
• The mathematical expression for this law is **F = m × a**, where **F** is the **force** applied, **m** is the **mass** of the body, and **a** is the **acceleration** produced. From this, the **acceleration** can be derived as **a = F / m**.
 
• In the first scenario provided in the question, the **force** is **F** and the **mass** is **m**, which results in an **acceleration** of **a = F / m**.
 
• In the second scenario, the **force** is increased to **3F** and the **mass** is reduced to **m/2**. To find the **new acceleration (a')**, we substitute these new values into the formula: **a' = (3F) / (m / 2)**.
 
• By performing the algebraic calculation, **a' = 3F × (2 / m)**, which simplifies to **a' = 6 × (F / m)**. Since the original **acceleration a** is **F / m**, the new value becomes **a' = 6a**.
 
• This demonstrates that increasing the **force** while simultaneously decreasing the **mass** leads to a significantly higher **acceleration**. *Hence, the statement that the new acceleration is 6a is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Force (F):** It is an external agency capable of changing the state of rest or motion of a particular body. It is a **vector quantity**, meaning it has both **magnitude** and **direction**. The **SI unit** of **force** is the **Newton (N)**, which is equivalent to **1 kg·m/s²**.
 
• **Mass (m):** This represents the quantity of **matter** contained in a body and serves as a measure of the body's **inertia**. Unlike weight, **mass** is a **scalar quantity** and remains constant regardless of the body's **location** in the universe. Its **SI unit** is the **kilogram (kg)**.
 
• **Acceleration (a):** It is defined as the **rate of change of velocity** with respect to **time**. If the **velocity** of an object changes, it is said to be accelerating. The **SI unit** for **acceleration** is **meters per second squared (m/s²)**.
 
• **Newton's Laws of Motion:** These **three laws** were first compiled by **Sir Isaac Newton** in his work **Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica**, published in **1687**. These laws form the basis for **classical mechanics** and describe the **physics** of moving objects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Inertia and Mass:** The **mass** of an object is a direct measure of its **inertia**. A larger **mass** requires more **force** to achieve the same **acceleration**. In this problem, reducing the **mass** to **m/2** effectively halved the resistance to change in motion, contributing to the increase in **acceleration**.
 
• **Proportionality:** The relationship shows that if **mass** is kept **constant**, **acceleration** is **doubled** when **force** is **doubled**. However, if **force** is kept **constant** and **mass** is **halved**, the **acceleration** also **doubles**. When both changes occur simultaneously as per the question (**3** times the **force** and **1/2** the **mass**), the total effect is **3 × 2 = 6**.
 
• **Practical Applications:** This principle is used in **automotive engineering** to design faster cars by either increasing **engine force (horsepower)** or using lightweight **materials** like **carbon fiber** to reduce the **mass** of the vehicle.
